headline: Vintage Boba Fett Auction Includes Historic Apology Note
post:
A rare vintage mail-away Boba Fett action figure is currently up for auction through Hakes, complete with its original cardboard mailer box, product catalogue, and a note to consumers from Kenner.

The included note offers a brief explanation regarding the removal of the figure's spring-launched rocket for safety reasons. This piece of Star Wars collecting history provides a fascinating look back at one of the hobby's most infamous unproduced features.

Is the rocket-firing Boba Fett your toy collecting holy grail?

#StarWars #BobaFett #ActionFigures
original_title: This Vintage Boba Fett Includes the Letter That Helped Create One of Star Wars Collecting’s Biggest Obsessions

headline: Famous Superheroes With Rough Comic Book Debuts
post:
Superhero history is full of iconic characters whose earliest appearances "offered little indication of the success awaiting them", according to Screen Rant. Many legendary heroes originally struggled to connect with readers or debuted as minor villains before finding their footing.

For instance, Wolverine first surfaced in 1974 as a Canadian government agent sent to capture the Hulk, long before joining the X-Men. Similarly, Frank Castle debuted as an armed antagonist hired to stop Spider-Man in 1974 before eventually starring in his own solo adventures.

Later writers and eventual screen adaptations completely transformed these rough launches into massive cultural phenomena. Did your favorite hero have a rocky start in the comics?

#Wolverine #Punisher #MarvelComics
original_title: 10 Famous Superheroes Who Were Complete Duds On Launch
